On Monday morning the shop opened late because the delivery van had broken down outside the depot, and the driver had to wait for a replacement part. While the staff sorted the backlog of orders, a customer arrived with a bicycle that had been sitting in her garage for years. The frame was sound, but the chain had rusted through and the rear wheel would not turn. We wrote up a ticket, explained what the repair would involve, and told her it would probably be ready by Thursday. In the afternoon the regional manager called to ask about the missing shipment, and we spent an hour going through the invoices line by line. It turned out that two boxes had gone to the wrong branch, so a courier was sent to collect them. By the end of the day the shelves were back in order, the staff had caught up with the paperwork, and the shop closed at the usual time.

On Tuesday the replacement part arrived, and the driver was able to finish his route before lunch. The branch manager asked us to review the stock counts, since the system had been showing numbers that did not match what was actually on the shelf. We spent the morning counting boxes and comparing them with the printout, and by noon we had found three discrepancies, all of them small. The owner of the bicycle called to ask whether the repair could be finished early, and we said we would try, though the wheel needed a new spoke and the rim had to be trued by hand. In the evening a few of the staff stayed behind to tidy the workroom, label the spare parts, and update the board where we keep track of jobs in progress. Nobody complained about the extra work, because the shop had been busy for weeks and everyone preferred to start the next morning with a clean bench.

On Wednesday the weather turned, and the rain kept most customers away, so we used the quiet hours to train the new apprentice on the till and on the procedure for returning defective goods to the supplier. She picked it up quickly, and by the end of the week she was handling the counter on her own. The week closed with the accounts balanced, the backlog cleared, and the van back on the road.
